summary:
# NOTES: Poppy Ott's Pedigreed Pickles (Leo Edwards, 1927, Grosset & Dunlap; illustrator Bert Salg)

Single book. Narrator: Jerry Todd (first person), chum Poppy Ott (long-legged, long-headed, "pickle" genius/promoter). Town: Tutter (La Salle County, Illinois), on river; "Zulutown" = tough end beyond Dad's brickyard. Street: Main Street; shop at 224 South Main Street. Poppy's father: Mr. Ott (runs Stilt factory; was a tramp, reformed). Poppy's mother dead. Jerry's parents: Mother, Dad (unnamed). Doc Leland (doctor, big nose glasses, Lizzie car). Bill Hadley, town marshal. Mr. Thomas Lorring, banker (Commercial Bank), helped stilt factory. Mr. Stair, Bid Stricker, Red Meyers, Denny Kirk, Spider Whickleberry (boy who rigged cat-strangling machine). Deacon Pillpopper (boat livery). Mr. Silas Hartenbower (102-year-old centenarian; told of pirate's lead cucumber mold). Mr. Wiggins (Wiggins & Wakefield, Rockford wholesaler); Henny (Poppy's Rockford cousin, wholesale grocery). Mr. Lorrimer (railroad president, dining car). Mr. Samson (railroad food buyer).

## Villains/antagonists
- **Mr. Foreman Pennykorn**: owner of Canners Exchange Bank (smallest, shabbiest of three Tutter banks) and Tutter Canning Company; stingy, "grasping," tight-fisted; wants Ashton plant bought; Dandy Dills pickles.
- **Norman Pennykorn**: his son, runs canning factory.
- **Forrest Pennykorn**: Norman's son, Foreman's grandson; "smarty," snob, sporty roadster; "monkey-face" insult; threatened Jerry.
- Cashier at bank: grumpy, suspicious (named Mr. Blynn).

## Mr. Simon Weckler
Stoop-shouldered widower, old, miser-reputed but donated assembly cabin to Boy Scout camp; thumps with heavy cane; yellow cat **Peter** (Poppy once fished him from dry cistern, bandaged foot). Housekeeper: **Mrs. Clayton**. Owns vacant lot across from canning factory; old summerhouse/playhouse in back yard (built for daughter Clara). Becomes Poppy's "silent partner"; asks $5/month or pay in pickles (2–3 quarts/mo). Daughter Clara eloped with Nathan Weir (nephew of pirate). Attacked in library by cat killer; cat Peter strangled; Weckler taken to hospital/operated, later recovers.

## Mrs. Cora O'Mally
Widow, pickle woman, lives in old Weir stone house in river bottoms (walls two feet thick, steep roof, huge chimney). Cucumber patch, "third year." Speaks Irish-brogue ("'Tis," "ye," "ould," "b'ys," "Mither of Moses"). Her pickles are the secret recipe (handed down ~100 years). Sold cucumbers to Poppy at $2/bushel; Pennykorn wanted 90¢. Ghost noises (tapping) in cellar; faints. Later marries Uncle Abner.

## Butch McGinty
Zulutown towing/house-mover, bachelor, hairy, red-nosed, dirty home (cat sleeping on table); mule **Jerusalem**; bakes burnt cookies; had been secretly making Mrs. O'Mally's recipe. Charged $10 to move store; hired at $3.50/day cash. Ruined batch (poison). Later steady job up canal, never returned.

## Uncle Abner Weir
Tommy's uncle, stern, whiskered "fringy" beard, cane, nightgown, false teeth, Bible-reader, from Rimtown, Ohio; "Uncle Ab." Later marries Mrs. O'Mally.

## Tommy Weir
Boy about their age, black hair, big black eyes, hot-tempered, strong grip; son of Nathan Weir and Clara Weckler (Clara's son → Mr. Weckler's grandson). Hid in cave with uncle across river (Weir canyon). Spoke with grandfather later; lives in old house near canning factory.

## Nathan Weir
Tommy's father; Ohio penitentiary (robbery, shot in arm, arm amputated); jewel robbery in Peoria accomplice; came to Tutter; one-armed cat killer; stole gold cucumber; died in hut/hospital. Pennykorn-affiliated? No—independent.

## Old Peg-leg Weir (pirate)
Built stone house; river pirate; preyed on St. Louis packet carrying gold; shot by posse; raised cucumbers as cover; made lead/gold cucumber mold; gold cucumber key given to Asa/Severn Weir's son (Abner's father). Hidden tunnel from creek "Weir creek" (Weir jungle) to cellar; secret iron/sheet-iron door in chimney base.

## Other characters: Mrs. Bowman (Elm St), Mrs. Morgan (616 Elm), Mrs. Hempline, Mrs. Cook (South Main), Mrs. Hiram Springer, Mrs. Brown (rotten pickle), Mrs. Bagley (broom), Mrs. Clayton, Miz Higgins (died after church supper poisoning), Cap'n Tinkertop (boat owner), Red Meyers.

# PLOT (in order)

1. Poppy proposes "Pickle Parlor"; Jerry sceptical; they go to Canners Exchange Bank; overhear Pennykorns discuss sweet corn ($9/ton vs Ashton $10.50), Dandy Dills, Ashton plant buy, cucumbers; Forrest rude. Store rent $125/mo (Pennykorn's empty building near Lattimer meat market). Poppy's "Pickle Parlor" oration to cashier.
2. Poppy's jar of pickles (bought at Presbyterian missionary food sale, Drake's store) – maker unknown. Poppy drops pickles at Parker grocery; sales-pitch oration to Mrs. Clayton. Visit Weckler; cat Peter; playhouse offered; Weckler "silent partner," pay in pickles.
3. Store painted green/yellow; ad "WHOSE PICKLES" with "Seven diamonds worth ten thousand dollars" (proofreader error). Sixty-three letters. Lorring bank account $100.
4. Calls on women; Peoria police chief telegram; Marshal Bill Hadley. Broom-swatting by woman. Jerry sick, Dad's pickles.
5. Jerry sick; Doc Leland; burglar in Poppy's cellar (pickles dumped). Butch McGinty found to be pickle genius. Poppy hires Butch ($3.50/day). "Aunt Jemima" scheme.
6. Mrs. O'Mally's farm: "Aunt Jemima" pickles; cucumbers $2/bushel (4 bushels); cellar sounds; she is frightened.
7. Forrest in truck tries to buy cucumbers; Mrs. O'Mally says two boys bought. Butch works in towed store; pickling begins; Mr. Ott & Poppy go to Rockford wedding; Jerry alone; 1,200 pickles in 300 bottles; "AUNT JEMIMA'S PICKLES" handbill; store moved to Mr. Weckler's lot, Pennykorns object.
8. Ptomaine poisoning across Tutter (church supper stuffed olives; Mrs. Higgins). Expense table: $100 → $32 left.
9. Mr. Weckler attacked in library; cat Peter strangled; gold cucumber found in flower bed; one-armed robber (handprint right only).
10. Poppy's order from Rockford (Wiggins) for two 30-gallon barrels; ordered Mrs. O'Mally's whole crop at $2/bushel (wrong, Pennykorn would have paid 90¢). 130 bushels in cellar.
11. Pennykorn visit to O'Mally; offers 90¢ (tiered $1/$0.90/$0.70). Forrest: "Monkey-face". Pennykorn threatens; deadline noon next day.
12. Tunnel search; Uncle Abner's cave; Tommy Weir; treasure hunt; Tommy caught by Poppy (fake sleep). Abner's story (Peg-leg). Cave shared by four.
13. Cucumber cellar; Mrs. Clayton; Pickles to Ladies' Aid (Methodist church); Lorring loan $500; "Pedigreed Pickles" name.
14. Two–three days of business; Pennykorn letter to Wiggins & Wakefield; farmer delivers cucumbers; Pennykorn offers contract; Poppy's trip to Chicago (Lorrimer railroad, Samson, hotels). Telegram: "Sold ten gallons to Chicago grocer..."
15. Bank confrontation: door locked; Poppy calls Bill Hadley through window; Poppy's orders > $6,000.
16. Gold cucumber key (two halves); moon/clock/chimney/coffin pictures; dig in shadow of chimney at midnight; iron chest found ~2 a.m.; treasure $35,000 total; each partner $7,000.
17. Lorring: Pennykorn deal; new pickle company; stock 50 shares apiece; Chamber of Commerce banquet; Poppy never said a word in speech. Tom & grandpa reunited. Abner marries Mrs. O'Mally. Nathan Weir died in hospital. Next book: POPPY OTT AND THE FRECKLED GOLDFISH.

# Other books in series listed at end (not part of story)
Poppy Ott: Stuttering Parrot; Seven-League Stilts; Galloping Snail; Pedigreed Pickles. Jerry Todd: Whispering Mummy; Rose-Colored Cat; Oak Island Treasure; Waltzing Hen; Talking Frog; Purring Egg; Whispering Cave.
